scale.same: Both tools ask for the same thing. Wording differs; the clinical answer does not.
scale.same-plus-dates: Same dose, and PneumoVax additionally gives the calendar date or checks the spacing of a dose already given - something PneumoRecs cannot do because it never asks for dates.
scale.differs: The two tools would lead a clinician to do different things.

why.I12: PneumoRecs says 'Schedule complete.' PneumoVax says one more dose is owed, because the third dose was given 30 days after the second and CDC's minimum there is 8 weeks. PneumoRecs is never told the dates, so it counts three doses and stops.
why.I13: An 11-month-old with no counting doses. PneumoRecs says 2 doses, PneumoVax says 3. Cause: PneumoRecs rounds a part-month UP when it picks the rulebook, so this child was handed the 12-23 month page. At exactly 11 months + 0 days the same tool says 3.
why.A02: 19-49 with HIV offered PCV15. PneumoVax recommends the PPSV23 at 8 weeks; PneumoRecs prints 'recommended at least 1 year, minimum 8 weeks can be considered'. ACIP's January 2025 table says 'administer ... at least 8 weeks' for this band; the tool is on its December 2024 text.
why.A07: Same split, for a patient whose PCV15 is already given - so the difference decides whether the PPSV23 is due today or in ten months.
why.X01: PneumoVax stops entirely for a stem-cell transplant, CAR-T or B-cell-depleting therapy and names the specialist protocols. PneumoRecs has no such question and gives the ordinary adult schedule. This is PneumoVax's owner decision of 2026-10-16, not an error on either side.
why.X02: A PCV20 dated in 2027. PneumoRecs counts it as given. PneumoVax rejects it and says why.
why.X03: A PCV15 given today. PneumoRecs says give the PPSV23 'to complete'; PneumoVax names the date it may first be given.
why.X04: Two PCV20 doses 14 days apart. PneumoRecs counts both and the schedule reads complete; PneumoVax rejects the second and still asks for dose 2.
why.X05: A PPSV23 three months after PCV13. PneumoRecs counts it; PneumoVax rejects it (an owner-set adult floor) and re-anchors the next dose.
why.X06: A PCV20 dated before the child was born. PneumoRecs counts it as a dose given before 12 months; PneumoVax rejects it. Both happen to end on one more dose.

wordingOnlyToReview.H02: A healthy 5-year-old with a completed 4-dose series: PneumoRecs says 'Schedule complete.', PneumoVax says 'Not indicated (healthy 5-18y)'. Same action (nothing to give) but PneumoVax does not acknowledge the completed series.
wordingOnlyToReview.A13: A 25-year-old with asplenia and a PCV20: PneumoVax says 'Complete'; PneumoRecs says no vaccine now and 'check this app when your patient turns 50'.
